MAJOR: Report persistence failure in `out()` is logged to stderr but the drill still exits 0; `status` will then report the drill stale/missing, silently converting an observability outage into a false DR-page — persist failure should fail the run (or at minimum be surfaced distinctly).

`CheckFreshness` returns on the first bad command, so an operator gets a partial picture (e.g. only `full` stale while `tenant`/`pitr` also stale); for an actionable DR readiness gate, aggregate all failures into one report.
Report files accumulate forever (`<command>-<ts>.json`, unbounded, no retention/pruning); a daily cadence across commands grows the directory indefinitely with no lifecycle policy.
MINOR: `require` is split on `,` without trimming, so `--require "full, tenant"` or trailing commas produce commands like `" tenant"` / `""`, yielding confusing `no  report in <dir>` errors; also empty `require` should be rejected explicitly.
`status` writes its own report via `out()`/`SaveReport` even though it is a meta-check; if `status` is ever added to `require` this becomes self-satisfying freshness.
`SaveReport` filename uses second-granularity timestamps; two runs in the same second silently overwrite, losing a drill record.
Default `--max-age-hours=26` and `--require full,tenant,pitr` bake in an operational assumption (daily cadence) that is not documented, validated, or reflected elsewhere in the tool.
No test for the stale-but-successful-report path, for `LatestReport` ordering across multiple files, or for failed-report short-circuit ordering — only happy/missing/failed cases are covered.

The diff does not visibly add/adjust tests or code for the PITR settings parsing, drill verification math, reconcile repair guard, and region routing criteria listed in the acceptance criteria; if those exist only from prior work, coverage should be confirmed and linked in the item.
NIT: `LatestReport` relies on lexicographic sort of the timestamped filename; correct today, but a comment noting the invariant would prevent a future format change from breaking ordering.
`out()` ignores the `json.MarshalIndent` error (`b, _ :=`), pre-existing but adjacent to the new code path.

`time.Duration(maxAgeHours*float64(time.Hour))` is subtly imprecise for fractional hours; fine in practice, but `time.Duration(maxAgeHours * float64(time.Hour))` with validation that maxAgeHours > 0 would be more defensive.
SUMMARY: Solid addition: per-drill persisted reports plus a `status` freshness gate is the right long-term shape for making DR drills continuously verifiable rather than a one-off exercise, and it stays in Go per the language rule.

Top risks: persistence failures don't fail the drill (false freshness), freshness checks stop at the first failure, and report files grow unbounded — all erode the trustworthiness of the DR readiness signal over time.
Recommend hardening before relying on `status` for alerting, and confirming acceptance-criteria coverage (PITR/drill/reconcile/region tests) is present and traceable.
